symptom: `create or modify business event service` of an existing service wrote a new random ChannelName for every message on every run: three runs of an unchanged script gave three different channel names, each reported `Modified business event service`. On a deployed app the ChannelName is the Kafka topic, so every re-run moves every topic and disconnects subscribers in other apps; mx check and the build stay clean.
cause: createBusinessEventService rebuilt the definition from the AST and called generateChannelName() for each message unconditionally, with no read of the stored channels. The canon $ID transplant cannot help: ChannelName is a content string, not an $ID, and no codec FreshGUIDField registration exists for it, so TestFreshGUIDFieldsHaveAnIdentityDecision never saw it (the same blind spot as Workflows PersistentId, #949).
fix: On a rewrite, carry the stored definition $ID and, per declared message matched by message name (case-insensitive), the stored channel's $ID and ChannelName, the message $ID, attribute $IDs (by attribute name) and the service-operation $ID; a new message gets a fresh channel name. A stored channel holding several messages (Studio Pro can; MDL writes one channel per message) is handed to the first message only, so no two channels share a topic (PR #533).
test: mdl/executor/cmd_businessevents_identity_test.go: TestCreateOrModifyBusinessEventService_CarriesChannelIdentity (MockBackend, Studio Pro-shaped IDs, reordered messages/attributes plus a new message and attribute), _SharedStoredChannelNotDuplicated, _RerunIsUnchanged (PedApp copy: run 2 writes no file, reports Unchanged, same ChannelNames). Revert control (carry fed nil): all three fail, the rerun with `re-run moved the channels` and the .mxunit + .mpr rewritten.
insight: An identity need not look like one: ChannelName is a plain string property, but something outside the model (the broker, other apps' subscriptions) remembers it, which is the definition canon.identityFields uses. Grep the executor for generate*/GenerateID calls on a CREATE OR MODIFY path — each is a candidate. Carry by name, not position, so reordering a script cannot swap topics; the end-to-end rerun test (files unchanged + Unchanged report) is what proves every other nested ID is also carried.
